title: Rajkumar Hirani Finally Made a Show. Nobody Can Agree If It's Good.
excerpt: Pritam and Pedro, Hirani's streaming debut on JioHotstar, has critics split down the middle — from 4-star raves to 'stunningly dull.' His son's acting debut isn't helping the consensus.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rajkumar Hirani's streaming debut, 'Pritam and Pedro', receives mixed reviews from critics.
  • Ratings range from 4 stars by NDTV to 2 stars from The Indian Express.
  • Vir Hirani's acting debut is met with divided opinions on his performance.
  • The show is available worldwide on JioHotstar with no geo-blocking.
  • Critics note a struggle between Hirani's traditional style and modern streaming demands.

Rajkumar Hirani doesn't fail. Not really. Not in the way that matters at the box office, not in the way critics remember. *3 Idiots*, *PK*, *Munna Bhai* — the man has an almost absurd track record of making films that are both critically beloved and commercially monstrous. He's Bollywood's designated genius, the one filmmaker even snobs and populists can agree on.

So when he finally stepped into streaming with Pritam and Pedro, a six-episode buddy-cop cybercrime series on JioHotstar, the expectations were specific: give us that Hirani warmth, that Hirani wit, but now with more room to breathe. For many in the diaspora, especially those who grew up watching his films, the prospect of a new Hirani project is always a significant event, often sparking family discussions across continents.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=uCjkRVV0-qU

Four days in, the reviews are all over the map. And the conversation isn't just about the show. It's about whether Bollywood's most trusted filmmaker has found his streaming legs — or tripped on them.

The Setup

The premise has that Hirani DNA: a mismatched duo, a crime with heart, a clash of old and new. Arshad Warsi plays Pedro, a grumpy, old-school Goan police inspector who gets punishment-posted to the cyber crime division after crossing a local politician. Vir Hirani — yes, the director's son, making his acting debut — plays Pritam, a mild-mannered vacuum salesman who also happens to be a computer genius. Together, they're tasked with solving the kidnapping of a chief minister's son, orchestrated by a sociopathic hacker named Martin, played by Vikrant Massey.

Boman Irani, Mona Singh, and Sanjay Dutt (in a cameo that Warsi teased at the premiere) round out the cast. Directed by Avinash Arun, who shot the gorgeous *Sacred Games* pilot, the show was created, co-written, and produced by Hirani alongside his longtime collaborator Abhijat Joshi.

> "The Quint was blunter: "No granularity."

The Verdict: Everyone Disagrees

Here's where it gets interesting.

![The Indian Express — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/8/85/Indian-Expree.jpg)

NDTV gave it 4 out of 5 stars, calling Warsi "excellent" and declaring Vir Hirani "leaves a lasting impression in his debut." Bollywood Hungama went with 3.5 stars, praising the "nail-biting narrative" and "fast-paced storytelling." The Hindu said Hirani "turns a cold, clinical cyber-thriller into a heartwarming buddy-cop comedy."

And then there's the other side.

The Indian Express gave it 2 out of 5, noting the show "fits right within the Rajkumar Hirani universe in which the baddies come with sad backstories and mitigation." Rediff also went with 2 stars, with Sukanya Verma writing that "Vir Hirani's stiff screen presence as Pritam has no vibe to match" Warsi's energy. The Quint was blunter: "No granularity. It is cybercrime explained at the level of a school assembly."

The harshest review came from The Hollywood Reporter India, where Suchin Mehrotra called it "a stunningly dull, bizarrely structured, tonally confused dud" and implored Hirani to "leave longform alone and stick to his strengths on the big screen."

Vir Hirani's Acting Debut: Mixed Reactions

›Rediff: 'Stiff screen presence.'

›General consensus: 'Fine, but not a revelation.'

The Son Question

Every review, positive or negative, circles the same elephant: Vir Hirani. This is a debut — and a loaded one. The son of India's most successful filmmaker, cast in the lead of his father's most high-profile project, on the country's biggest streaming platform.

The reviews suggest he's... fine. NDTV is kind. Rediff finds him stiff. THR says he "struggles to register with odd, over-rehearsed diction." Nobody's calling him a revelation, but nobody's calling him a disaster either. The truth is probably that he's a young actor with potential who's been placed in a role that demands someone with Warsi's effortless comic timing as a scene partner — a nearly impossible benchmark for anyone's first outing.

The Bigger Picture

There's a meta-narrative that several critics have noticed: a filmmaker known for two-hour crowd-pleasers trying to stretch into an eight-hour streaming format mirrors the show's own plot — an old-school cop trying to navigate a new-age digital world. Both are fish-out-of-water stories.

For the diaspora, Pritam and Pedro is available worldwide on JioHotstar — no geo-blocking, no waiting for an international release window. If you have a subscription, you can stream all six episodes right now. The show is in Hindi with subtitles available, making it accessible to a wide range of NRI viewers, including those who may not be fluent in Hindi but want to stay connected to Indian entertainment. Early reactions from NRI social media groups show a similar split to critics, with some praising its nostalgic Hirani feel and others wishing for a more modern, fast-paced thriller.

Whether you'll love it depends on which Hirani you're looking for. If you want the broad, heartfelt, slightly sentimental Hirani who made *3 Idiots* — you might find it. If you want the kind of sharp, layered, propulsive streaming television that the best Indian series have delivered (think *Scam 1992* or *Paatal Lok*) — you might find it wanting. Either way, you'll have an opinion. And with Hirani, that's never been a given before. His films usually just... worked. This one has people talking, arguing, and watching anyway.

Which might be exactly what JioHotstar is counting on.
